text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

The clinical picture of a preterm infant (32 weeks) born via C-section with ground-glass opacities on X-ray and respiratory acidosis is classic for RDS, likely exacerbated by lack of surfactant production in preterm lungs. The cesarean delivery may have contributed by preventing lung fluid clearance.
